tasks.title: forge history reads the committed events
tasks.objective: Add a forge history command that reads .factory/events.jsonl, filtered by story, event type, or date range, and shows events with no story attribution rather than hiding them — the reader the 314 committed events currently lack.
acceptance_criteria: load_events gains event= (type) and since=/until= (date, ISO prefix) filters alongside the existing story=, and each composes with the others.
forge history with no filter prints every event, grouping by story and printing an explicit section for events that carry no story, so a gap is shown rather than filtered away.

forge history --story <key>, --event <type>, --since <date> and --until <date> each narrow the output as named, and event types are discovered from the data rather than validated against a hardcoded set.
The command is read-only: it opens events.jsonl for reading only and writes nothing, proven by asserting no write occurs against a repo whose .factory is otherwise untouched.
forge history is registered in forge.py and runs stdlib-only.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "history or events"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That event types are discovered, not enumerated — a hardcoded set would silently drop any new type an emitter adds. And that the reader truly never writes: no lazy 'append missing field' or file rewrite hiding in the read path.

tasks.title: Quickfix windows record what they touched
tasks.objective: Make an open quickfix window record every product file written through it, including inside an approved story where guard_product_writes returns early today, while keeping the five-file budget binding only where the quickfix is the sole authorization.
acceptance_criteria: When a quickfix window is open, every product path a write touches is recorded against the window BEFORE the approved-plan early return in guard_product_writes, so a window opened during an active story records its files instead of recording nothing.
Recording is passive: it appends to the window's file list, reaches no deny, and returns no authorization — the planning lock's deny paths and the approved-plan early return are otherwise unchanged.
The five-file budget (claim_files) still binds on the path where the quickfix is the sole authorization: an unplanned write of a sixth distinct file is still refused.
A quickfix opened inside an approved, decomposed story ends with a non-empty files list after a product write — the exact case that recorded nothing before.
The recording is idempotent: the same file touched twice appears once.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "quickfix or guard or claim"
tasks.reviewer_focus: This edits pre_tool_use.py, the always-armed planning lock (0013). The one thing that matters: recording must add a RECORD, never an authorization. Verify every deny path still fires and the recording branch cannot cause a write to be allowed that would otherwise be denied. If the recording path can skip a deny, that is a blocking finding.

tasks.title: The PR link is an event
tasks.objective: Link a merged PR to the work it shipped by appending a pr-linked event to .factory/events.jsonl — the one durable home that survives a clone with no GitHub remote — surfaced by forge history.
acceptance_criteria: forge pr-link records a pr-linked event carrying the story/issue key and the PR reference, appended to .factory/events.jsonl through append_event.
forge history shows the pr-linked event for its story, so 'which PR shipped this' is answered from committed data with no GitHub call.
The link is readable after a clone with no remote configured: a test reads it back with no origin set.
The PR reference is not written to run.json, because pr_ready reduces run.json to {project, phase} and would erase it at ship.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "pr_link or history"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That the event is the ONLY home — no parallel write to run.json or a sidecar that a clone or a ship would drop. The whole point is one durable place, verified to survive with no remote.

tasks.title: The record states where it begins, and no shipped story is silently outcome-less
tasks.objective: Write a record-origin boundary marker at init and adopt (date, commit, count of preceding commits), have the board report it instead of implying completeness, add the two pre-contract stories to the roadmap MARKED as predating the outcome contract, and have doctor report any done story that is both unmarked and outcome-less.
acceptance_criteria: forge init and forge adopt write .factory/record-origin.json with date, commit, and preceding_commits (the count of commits already in the repo), create-if-absent so a re-adopt never rewrites the origin.
The boundary marker lives in its own committed file, NOT run.json, so pr_ready's {project, phase} projection cannot erase it at first ship.

The board API (aggregate_state) carries record-origin.json AND index.html renders the boundary ('record begins here; N commits precede it') rather than implying the project began at adoption; when the marker is absent (a repo predating this) the board says nothing false.

FORGE-INIT-1 and harness-v2-wedge appear in plans/roadmap.json as done items carrying predates_outcome_contract: true, their epic (symphony-forge — real structural membership, which the roadmap contract requires of every item), and NO outcome field. Key, title, status and epic are reconstructed from committed evidence; the OUTCOME is never synthesised — that is the honesty rule, and epic membership is a fact, not an outcome.
forge doctor REPORTS any done roadmap item that is both outcome-less and unmarked; the check is a report, not a load-time gate, so a legacy roadmap still loads (the PH-2 authoring-not-loading rule).
docs/getting-started.md and factory/skills/forge.md describe forge history and the record boundary.
verify_commands: uv run --with pytest python -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "origin or boundary or predates or doctor or board"
tasks.reviewer_focus: That no outcome is synthesised for the two pre-contract stories — they carry a marker and nothing else, which is the spec's honesty rule. And that the doctor check is a report, not a gate: adding it to load_roadmap or save_roadmap would refuse a legacy client roadmap, the exact PH-2 mistake.
